mcqs.q: Using the Shelter Quality Protocol in Brazilian long-term shelters, the predominant shelter-management welfare hazards were:
o: Lack of rehoming/admission policies, preventive healthcare, and trained staff
Overcrowding caused by excessively high adoption rates
mcqs.e: Management hazards centered on absent rehoming/admission policies, preventive healthcare programs, and trained staff.

mcqs.q: Which environmental hazards did the study flag in the shelter housing?
o: Bedding inadequacy and surfaces difficult to keep clean
Adequate rehabilitation programs but small enclosures
Low stocking density with high enrichment
mcqs.e: Environmental hazards included inadequate bedding, hard-to-clean surfaces, behavioral problems, and lack of rehabilitation programs.

mcqs.q: What standardized instrument was used to evaluate the 588 dogs and 201 enclosures?
mcqs.e: The welfare assessment was conducted with the Shelter Quality Protocol.

mcqs.q: What was the study's overall conclusion about predicting successful dog adoptions?
o: Dog personality alone reliably predicts adoption success
Human and dog personality showed strong matching correlations
Personality (dog or human) alone cannot sufficiently determine successful adoption
mcqs.e: The authors concluded adoption success is multifactorial and personality alone is insufficient.

mcqs.q: How strong were the correlations between human and dog personality domains?
mcqs.e: Spearman coefficients (-0.11 to 0.16) showed only weak human-dog personality associations.

mcqs.q: How was the dog Training Focus domain related to human-animal attachment (LAPS)?
o: Attachment decreased as Training Focus increased
Attachment increased as Training Focus increased
Motivation, not Training Focus, was the strongest predictor
mcqs.e: Higher dog Training Focus was associated with higher owner attachment scores.

mcqs.q: What had the strongest influence on dogs' stress levels during handling?
o: Increasing familiarity with the setting and the handler
Time of day the session occurred
mcqs.e: Stress measures improved as dogs became more familiar with the setting and handler across handling sets.

mcqs.q: What did the study find regarding emotional contagion between dogs and unfamiliar handlers?
o: No consistent support for emotional contagion was found
Contagion increased with each handling set
mcqs.e: The brief contact yielded no consistent evidence of dog-handler emotional contagion.

mcqs.q: From the first to the third handling set, canine heart rate variability (RMSSD):
mcqs.e: HRV (RMSSD) rose significantly by set 3, indicating reduced stress with familiarity.

mcqs.q: Into which three major categories did the review group canine behavioral test stimuli?
mcqs.e: The dog-centric framework grouped 29 subcategories into human-oriented, environmental, and motivator-oriented stimuli.

mcqs.q: What was the review's main conclusion about behavioral testing methods?
o: No common features exist across protocols
Despite heterogeneity, common stimuli emerged, yielding a practical framework
Only one valid test type exists
mcqs.e: Methodological heterogeneity persisted but common stimuli allowed a practical organizing framework.

mcqs.q: Which four new behavior domains did the modified (WDC-BARQ) questionnaire add?
mcqs.e: EFA extracted four new working-dog domains: Playfulness, Impulsivity, Distractibility, and Basophobia (plus Food focus).

mcqs.q: What did the authors conclude about the WDC-BARQ?
o: It successfully expands the C-BARQ for working dog populations
The original C-BARQ already captured all relevant domains
mcqs.e: The modified instrument extended C-BARQ measurement to dimensions relevant to working dogs.

mcqs.q: In this study, 'Basophobia' refers to fear of:
mcqs.e: Basophobia was defined as fear of falling.

mcqs.q: Which Assistance Dog Test Battery model best predicted working outcomes?
mcqs.e: The 10-week model (AUC 0.84) substantially outperformed the 3-week model and prior state-of-the-art.

mcqs.q: What practical benefit did the authors propose for assistance dog organizations?
o: Reducing training costs by guiding which dogs to withdraw
mcqs.e: Model predictions can guide early withdrawal decisions, lowering training costs.

mcqs.q: The 10-week ADTB model predicted outcomes with an AUC of approximately:
mcqs.e: The 10-week model achieved an ROC AUC of 0.84 (vs 0.74 at 3 weeks).

mcqs.q: When the UK guide-dog Puppy Profiling Assessment was applied to the US (GDB) population, what was found?
o: No subtest provided predictive value for ultimate success
The same five subtests predicted success as in the UK
Only the noise subtest predicted success
mcqs.e: Unlike the UK findings, no subtest predicted guide-dog success in the US population.

mcqs.q: What does the study imply about standardized working-dog behavior tests?
o: They must be re-validated across different programs and populations
Puppy age is irrelevant to results
mcqs.e: Failure to generalize highlights the need to re-assess test validity across programs.

mcqs.q: What did the study reveal about error in citizen-science behavior testing?
o: Citizen-science error is always random and evens out
Tester identity was associated with outcomes, indicating systematic error
Citizen scientists matched trained researchers exactly
Large sample size eliminated all error
mcqs.e: Tester (citizen vs trained) was linked to outcomes, so error was not purely random.

mcqs.q: What did the authors recommend in response to these findings?
o: Introduce controls/quality checks to detect tester effects
mcqs.e: Quality checks and preliminary analyses are needed to catch systematic tester effects.

mcqs.q: In which tests was tester identity associated with outcomes?
o: The Alone Time Test and the Three-Toy Test
mcqs.e: Tester effects appeared specifically in the Alone Time Test and the Three-Toy Test.

journal: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science

mcqs.q: How did the presence of people in the room affect enrichment item use by colony cats?
mcqs.e: People being present significantly reduced use across all enrichment categories.

mcqs.q: Cats seized or signed over from hoarding/cruelty cases preferentially used which enrichment type?
mcqs.e: Hoarding/cruelty-case cats used enclosed (security) spaces more.

mcqs.q: As length of stay increased, cats used more of which enrichment?
mcqs.e: Use of vertical (vantage) surfaces rose with longer time in the shelter.

mcqs.q: How were hair (HCC) and nail (NCC) cortisol concentrations related in cats?
mcqs.e: HCC and NCC were significantly associated (rs = 0.70).

mcqs.q: Cats with litterbox issues showed which cortisol pattern?
mcqs.e: Litterbox issues were associated with significantly higher hair and nail cortisol.

mcqs.q: What was the clinical takeaway regarding these cortisol measures?
o: HCC is the single most reliable stress measure
NCC may improve chronic-stress detection, while HCC variability warrants caution
Cortisol cannot be measured in cats
mcqs.e: NCC showed promise for identifying chronic stress; HCC varied widely, urging caution.

mcqs.q: What was the key finding about cats and the Kanizsa (illusory) square?
o: Cats selected the Kanizsa illusion about as often as the real square
mcqs.e: Cats sat in illusory contours as often as real squares and more than controls.

mcqs.q: What did the authors interpret from this result?
o: Cats may treat subjective Kanizsa contours as if they were real contours
mcqs.e: Equal selection of illusion and real square suggests cats perceive subjective contours like real ones.

mcqs.q: What study method was used?
o: Citizen science with owners testing cats at home
mcqs.e: It was a COVID-era citizen-science study with owners running trials at home.

mcqs.q: How did indoor-only cats compare to indoor-outdoor cats in predatory play?
o: Indoor-only cats approached and played with prey-like stimuli sooner
mcqs.e: Indoor-only cats engaged the artificial prey stimuli sooner than indoor-outdoor cats.

mcqs.q: Cats raised with their mother for a longer duration showed:
mcqs.e: Longer maternal rearing was linked to fewer failed attempts catching the chaser.

mcqs.q: What broader implication did the findings support?
o: Predatory interest requires prior live-prey experience
Indoor-only cats retain predatory play interest despite no live-prey experience
Outdoor access is required for any play
Play drive is unrelated to housing
mcqs.e: Prey-deprived indoor cats still showed strong interest in prey-like stimuli.
